subsystems.name: Photon source
subsystems.role: produces the quantum states that carry the key.
parts: attenuated laser (weak coherent pulses, the common case)
entangled photon-pair source or chip-based source

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: carries single photons without letting anyone copy them unnoticed.
parts: dark optical fibre at telecom wavelengths

subsystems.name: Single-photon detection
subsystems.role: registers individual photons with precise timing.
parts: superconducting nanowire detectors or avalanche photodiodes

subsystems.name: Classical post-processing
subsystems.role: turns raw detections into a short, secret key.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: stores keys and feeds them to encryption equipment.
parts: interfaces to AES or one-time-pad encryptors

subsystems.name: Trusted relay nodes
subsystems.role: extend range beyond what one fibre span allows, at the cost of trusting each node.

buildSteps.title: Pick the protocol
buildSteps.detail: Most deployments use BB84 prepare-and-measure with decoy pulses; entanglement-based variants (E91, BBM92) are used where a source can be shared.

buildSteps.title: Build the transmitter
buildSteps.detail: A laser is attenuated to well below one photon per pulse on average, or a nonlinear crystal generates entangled pairs; the state is encoded in polarisation, phase or time bin.

buildSteps.title: Lay the quantum channel
buildSteps.detail: Dedicated dark fibre at 1550 nm is installed and kept free of strong classical traffic where possible, with polarisation or phase drift compensated actively.

buildSteps.title: Install detectors
buildSteps.detail: Single-photon detectors are mounted at the far end, shielded and cooled, with timing electronics tuned to reject noise.

buildSteps.title: Implement post-processing
buildSteps.detail: Software sifts matching bases, corrects errors and compresses the remaining bits by hashing so an eavesdropper's partial knowledge is squeezed out.

buildSteps.title: Authenticate the classical channel
buildSteps.detail: Each link needs an initial pre-shared secret or certificate, because without it a man-in-the-middle can impersonate the receiver.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryption
buildSteps.detail: The distilled keys are delivered to AES or one-time-pad encryptors carrying real traffic, with key refresh rates matched to demand.

buildSteps.title: Extend with relays or repeaters
buildSteps.detail: Beyond roughly a few hundred kilometres of fibre, signals are either regenerated at trusted nodes or, in research, held in quantum memories.

prerequisites.why: without them the raw key rate collapses and errors swamp the link.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss telecom fibre and stable optics
prerequisites.why: fibre loss caps the distance a photon can travel before it is simply gone.
QKD only secures the key; the reconciliation channel must already be trustworthy.
they are the only way to beat fibre loss without trusting intermediate nodes.
buyers need proven interoperability and security claims before large-scale rollout.

pathway.milestone: metro QKD links and trusted-node backbones, plus satellite distribution demonstrated (Micius, 2016; the Beijing–Shanghai trunk line, 2017)
pathway.unlocks: key distribution between fixed sites where fibre exists and relays can be secured.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale QKD modules and published standards from bodies such as ETSI
pathway.unlocks: cheaper links that can plug into ordinary network equipment.

pathway.milestone: device-independent and measurement-device-independent protocols in the field
pathway.unlocks: security that no longer rests on trusting the hardware's calibration.

pathway.milestone: quantum repeaters linking many nodes into an entanglement network
pathway.unlocks: long-distance key distribution without trusted relays — though post-quantum cryptography, standardised in 2024, will likely cover most near-term needs first.
